title: How IXOM centralised its emissions data ahead of ASRS assurance
summary: IXOM, with around 1,300 staff in more than 50 locations, brought its emissions data into one place and has processed 679 files through the Data Transformation Agent, with source evidence kept on file for ASRS assurance.
body_markdown:
[IXOM](https://www.linkedin.com/company/ixom/) operates in more than 50 locations across Australia, New Zealand, the US and parts of Asia, with around 1,300 staff. Its emissions data came in from different teams across the business, and IXOM wanted a more centralised way to manage it.


Under Australia's mandatory climate reporting rules (ASRS), those numbers also have to be ready for assurance, an independent check of the figures.


### One platform, organised around the business


We worked through IXOM's existing processes with their team, then set up a centralised platform for emissions data management across IXOM's operations, organised around how the company is structured.


### 679 files processed, with the evidence kept


Since December 2025, IXOM has processed 679 files through our Data Transformation Agent, including electricity and water invoices that would otherwise be reformatted by hand, and the agent keeps the source evidence on file for assurance as it goes. The Gap Analyzer then showed the sustainability team where its climate disclosures were already well developed and where they could go further.


### What changed for the team


[Gerald Yeo](https://www.linkedin.com/in/gerald-yeo-976ab384/) , IXOM's Sustainability Coordinator, describes what changed:


> "The platform is intuitive to use and the level of integration and centralisation has streamlined our emissions reporting process. We now have greater visibility and insights into our environmental performance."


For a company reporting under ASRS for the first time, an inventory that sits in one place with its evidence attached is a much easier starting point when the auditor arrives.
